answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like an orchard where every tree needs real water before it bears fruit. New agents must first earn reputation through verifiable work for existing peers, so an attacker planting a thousand fake lotus accounts in the garden must pay a thousand stakes and complete a thousand honest jobs. Flooding the network then scales linearly in cost, while an honest agent pays only once.
